name: Purify water using several methods
blurb: Knowing three independent ways to make water safe — and their limits — is one of the genuinely life-saving skills on this list.
steps: Learn the source hierarchy: flowing water above human activity beats standing water; a spring beats a stream.
Pre-filter sediment through cloth or by letting it settle — every method works better on clear water.
Boiling: a rolling boil for one minute kills everything biological. Three minutes above 2,000 m. It does not remove chemicals.
Filtration: understand pore size. A 0.2 micron filter handles bacteria and protozoa but not viruses.
Chemical treatment: chlorine dioxide or iodine, respecting the contact times, which lengthen dramatically in cold water.
Practise the full sequence in the field, including how you keep dirty and clean containers separate.
tips: No method covers everything. Filters miss viruses, chemicals miss cryptosporidium, boiling misses chemicals.
Cross-contamination is the usual real-world failure: dirty threads, dirty hands, dirty lid.
proof: You can explain what each method does and does not kill, and treat water three different ways in the field.
